unit.title: Preparing for the Oral History Interview

contentBlocks.text: This week you built every piece needed for a real, respectful oral-history interview. Today, put it all together in a mock practice run.

Quick review: a good question is open-ended, not yes/no (Day 1). A strong question list moves through ਬਚਪਨ, ਜਵਾਨੀ, and adulthood in order (Day 2). ਧਿਆਨ ਨਾਲ ਸੁਣਨਾ means following what's said and asking real follow-ups, not just reading a list (Day 3). Genuine ਇਜਾਜ਼ਤ, asked respectfully, always comes first (Day 4). Practice a short mock interview with a family member or partner: ask your permission sentence, then ask two questions from your Day 2 list, listening for one real follow-up opportunity.
You're now genuinely ready to conduct your real interview. This preparation — questions, listening, and respect — is the foundation the rest of this year's documentary capstone builds on.

objectives: Synthesize the week's four skills — open questions, organization, active listening, consent — into one practice interview
Conduct a short mock interview using real Day 2 questions and a genuine follow-up
materialsNeeded: A family member or partner to practice with
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child conduct a short mock interview with a family member or partner, using their own permission sentence and two Day 2 questions.
3. Complete the cumulative review worksheet, reflecting on the mock interview.
4. Discuss what went well and what to adjust before the real interview.
5. Celebrate finishing the first full week — this preparation is the foundation for the whole year's capstone.
differentiationTips: Struggling: allow the mock interview to be shorter (one question) and focus reflection on just one skill at a time
Ready for more: ask them to identify one moment in the mock interview where a genuine, unplanned follow-up question naturally arose
This is a good checkpoint to note which skill (question quality, organization, listening, or consent) needs the most reinforcement before the real interview
teacherGuide.answerKey: A complete answer reflects on a real mock interview: which questions were asked, whether a genuine follow-up arose, and how the permission request went — content varies by student, evaluated against genuine engagement with all four skills.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates the week's four interview-preparation skills before the capstone project moves to the real interview, matching the 'consolidate before adding more' pacing established across this session.
